page.layout: One block of Latin verse in italic, full width, at the top; below it a full-width German title in black letter; below that a German verse stanza in black letter; the catchword and signature at the foot right and centre. No marginal notes.

l.i: Nam quid adhuc superest? si te neq; provocat
O bis marmoreum pectus! neq; mitigat unquam
Si neq; tantarum vel spes certissima rerum
Si neq; tartarea cohibet formido Gehennæ:
Imò si durant magis hæc adduntq; stuporem
Vt facile immanesq; feras, chalybémq;, petramq;
Quid faciat pietas, quibus artibus abstrahat
Invitum servare nec est mentis puto

l.bl: Kind-leins Jesu an den Sünder/ gezo-
Jeweil bey mir allein man findet/
Wie thöricht ist/ der anderst wo Die

page.notes: The parenthesis-like mark "(dens," at the end of the second Latin line is doubtful; it may be a stray or a partly printed word. The Latin verse block is treated as one stanza. Underlining under "Quid faciat pietas" is in the print. Long s is plain s throughout; u/v is normalised by vowel/consonant function ("vnd" to "und", "Inuitum" to "Invitum", "seruare" to "servare"). Black letter is marked with bl, since it appears within a roman and italic page. Hyphen at line end "Kind-leins" and "gezo-gen" kept as printed.
